small_guidance:
- The current kernel re-loads each input pixel for every (oc, dy, dx) combination and stores a BLOCK_OC×BLOCK_P accumulator that is mostly bias-padded. Restructure the inner loop so that for each (ic, kh, kw) you load the input patch once into a shared register tile of shape [BLOCK_P, POOL*POOL] (or just sum the POOL×POOL window into a single [BLOCK_P] vector), then do one outer product with wv[:, None]. This cuts redundant gmem traffic by ~POOL² (=16×).
- Expand the autotune grid with larger BLOCK_P (256, 512) and smaller BLOCK_OC (8, 16) since OC=64 and PH*PW=96*96=9216 — the spatial tile is where parallelism lives. Try num_warps=8, num_stages=3 with BLOCK_P=512.
- Replace the final `tl.atomic_add(out_ptr + pid_n, s)` contention point by having one program per N (grid axis 0) accumulate into a local scratch and only atomic-add once per program; or use a two-stage reduction (write per-(n, oc-tile, p-tile) partials, then a tiny reduction kernel) to avoid atomics altogether.
large_guidance:
- Reformulate as an im2col-style GEMM where the K dimension is IC*KH*KW and the M dimension is OC, but iterate output positions at the *pooled* granularity: each program owns one (N, OC tile, pooled-spatial tile). Inside, for each pooled position, sum the POOL×POOL pre-conv input window per (ic, kh, kw) into one scalar (this is legitimate — it is summing input pixels feeding the same pooled output, not pre-reducing weights), then do a single MAC per (kh, kw, ic). This keeps the full MAC count (OC·N·PH·PW·IC·KH·KW) but eliminates the POOL² redundant outer-product work.
- Fuse bias-add, divide-by-POOL², sigmoid, and the (oc, ph, pw) reduction entirely inside the kernel epilogue using tl.sum across both axes, and write one partial per (n, oc-tile, p-tile) into a small scratch buffer; a second tiny kernel (or torch.sum) reduces over those tiles. This avoids the global atomic_add hotspot on a length-N output.
- Consider channels-last (NHWC) input layout so the IC axis is contiguous — the K-loop in the GEMM then issues fully coalesced loads. Pre-permute weight to (OC, KH, KW, IC) once at init (constant rewrite, not algebraic shortcut) so the inner-product over IC is a contiguous dot.
